long_biography.plain_text:
Thomas Evangeliou brought banking experience to the small cotton-bud business behind Septona. He arranged borrowing to expand production, while the company brought sticks, cotton components and packaging under its own manufacturing operation. It also made goods for retailers’ own labels, gaining shelf space without bearing the full promotional cost of launching its brand abroad.

At an early trade fair in Amsterdam, Evangeliou took a friend to translate because he did not speak English. He returned to international exhibitions to find customers, presenting Greek cotton as a competitive raw material. The export business grew through relationships with distributors and retailers.
